passage: In a small flat in Toronto, Xin, two and a half, watched Dad rock baby Nadia and hold her rattle. Xin marched over and snatched it. Nadia wailed. Dad didn't call him selfish. "You want Dad too," he said. "Nadia has the rattle now. Xin has the drum. Then it's Xin and Dad and the truck book, just us." Xin banged the drum twice, glanced at Dad, and climbed onto his lap with the book.

qa.q: What did Xin snatch from Nadia?
What might Xin have wanted when he grabbed the rattle?
qa.a: He may have felt left out and wanted to know he still mattered to Dad now that the baby got so much attention.

qa.q: Why did Dad's response work better than calling Xin selfish?
qa.a: It gave Xin his own turn and some one-on-one time without shaming him for what he did. 🙂

qa.q: What was the moment like for Nadia?
qa.a: Nadia was a baby who suddenly lost her rattle, so she was startled and upset, and she needed comfort too.

grounding: Shows an older toddler grabbing a baby's toy out of jealousy and parents giving separate turns and one-on-one time.

"Mine!" Rafiq, three, grabbed the rattle from baby Darshan.

Darshan wailed. Their mother picked up the baby. "Rafiq!"

Rafiq's chin wobbled. "Baby has everything."

His mother paused. She gave Darshan to Abbu. Then she knelt. "Rafiq, come. Just you and me. Let's read your truck book."

Rafiq climbed onto her lap.

"Later, baby gets a turn with the rattle. Now it's your turn with me."

qa.q: What did Rafiq grab from baby Darshan?
What does Rafiq's wobbling chin and "Baby has everything" suggest?
qa.a: It suggests Rafiq felt jealous and left out, wondering whether he still mattered.

qa.q: What did the mother do instead of shaming Rafiq?
qa.a: She gave him one-on-one time with his truck book and set separate turns for the rattle.

qa.q: How does baby Darshan experience the moment?
qa.a: Darshan is upset and wails when the rattle is grabbed, and is comforted by being held.

grounding: Shows an older toddler grabbing from the baby out of jealousy, and a parent giving one-on-one time and separate turns instead of shaming.

passage:
Childminder's note, Monday.

Tushar, three, snatched the soft ball from baby Ishita twice today and watched to see what I would do.

I didn't call him selfish. I gave Ishita a rattle and took Tushar to the window for ten minutes to count buses, just the two of us.

After that he played beside her calmly. At pickup I suggested his parents try a little special time with him each day.

qa.q: What did Tushar snatch from baby Ishita?
Why might Tushar have watched to see what the childminder would do?
qa.a: Tushar may have felt jealous and unsure, testing whether he still mattered when the baby got attention.

qa.q: What approach did the childminder use, and why did it work?
qa.a: The childminder avoided shaming him and gave him ten minutes of one-on-one time, which calmed his jealousy.

qa.q: How might Tushar's parents feel about the suggestion at pickup?
qa.a: They may feel relieved to have a simple plan, and perhaps a bit surprised at how much Tushar needs special time.

grounding: Shows an older toddler grabbing toys from the baby to test whether he still matters, met with one-on-one time instead of shame.
